vintage: Levels use one ALFRED vintage for the whole history. Earlier observations include revisions known by the vintage date. Dates label observation months, not publication dates. Only closed calendar months are shown. Missing levels or comparison months yield null.

unemployment.label: Unemployment rate
unemployment.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED / ALFRED
unemployment.definition: Seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for the civilian labor force aged 16 and over.

cpi.label: Consumer price index
cpi.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED / ALFRED
cpi.definition: Seasonally adjusted all-items index for urban consumers, U.S. city average.

cpiYoY.label: Consumer price inflation
cpiYoY.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED / ALFRED
cpiYoY.definition: Percentage change from the same month one year earlier in the seasonally adjusted all-items CPI index. BLS conventionally reports headline 12-month inflation from its unadjusted index.

industrialProduction.label: Industrial production
industrialProduction.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, via FRED / ALFRED
industrialProduction.definition: Seasonally adjusted index of real output in manufacturing, mining and utilities.

industrialProductionYoY.label: Industrial production growth
industrialProductionYoY.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, via FRED / ALFRED
industrialProductionYoY.definition: Percentage change from the same month one year earlier in the seasonally adjusted industrial production index.

recession.label: NBER recession
recession.definition: Computed from NBER turning-point dates. Months after a peak through the trough are 1. Other classified months are 0. Dating is retrospective and recent months can be reclassified.

sourceNotes.recessionAttribution: Own monthly calculation from NBER business-cycle peak and trough dates, checked against the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis USREC vintage.
